idea-plugin.name: Caret IME
idea-plugin.description:
Switches the input method automatically based on where the caret is: English in code, Chinese in comments and in Chinese string literals, and the caret is tinted with the comment colour so the current mode is visible at a glance.

String literals are judged by content — a literal that already contains Chinese, or a freshly typed empty "" with the caret between the quotes, counts as Chinese; an ASCII-only literal such as "userId" is treated as code. If you switch the IME yourself, the plugin backs off inside that comment or string until the caret moves elsewhere, and it never injects a keystroke while an IME composition is still in flight.

Windows only. It switches the IME by injecting keystrokes — a decoy F24 press/release followed by a Shift press/release. The IMM32 write API (ImmSetOpenStatus) has no effect on TSF-based input methods such as Microsoft Pinyin, so simulating keys is the only way to switch them. The F24 decoy exists to stop IntelliJ IDEA from mistaking the rapidly injected Shift keystrokes for a "double Shift" (the Search Everywhere shortcut) when the caret sweeps back and forth across a comment boundary.

Tested only on Windows 11 + IntelliJ IDEA 2025.2 + Microsoft Pinyin. Other platforms and input methods are untested.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.1.0
  • String literals now count as Chinese context: a literal that already contains Chinese, or a freshly typed empty "" with the caret between the quotes, switches to Chinese. ASCII-only literals such as "userId" are still treated as code.
  • No more interference while you type: the plugin now detects an in-progress IME composition and does not inject any keystroke, so typing Chinese is never interrupted.
  • The plugin now backs off when you switch the IME yourself — it stops switching inside that comment or string until the caret moves elsewhere.
1.0.0
  • First public release.
  • Automatically switches the input method based on the caret position — Chinese inside comments, English inside code.
  • Tints the caret with the comment colour while it sits inside a comment.
  • Injects an F24 decoy key so the switch never triggers IntelliJ IDEA's "double Shift" (Search Everywhere).
